4.text: The skins of small seals that are used with the hair on are prepared by

5.text: merely scraping their inner side with an iron scraper. A little blubber which

6.text: is left on the skin helps to make it softer. These skins are not dyed, and

7.text: are used for spring boots and trousers, also for bags

8.text: of every kind. The seal-skin trousers and boots are

9.text: very tough, and wear much better than those of

10.text: reindeer-skin, especially in damp weather, for they

11.text: are not spoiled when dried after being wet.

12.text: The skins prepared for summer boots are folded

13.text: wet, with the hair side in, and allowed to lie for a

14.text: night or two. Then they are well scraped on both

15.text: sides. To make the skin black it is rubbed with coal

16.text: mixed with oil, or sometimes with the black dust

17.text: gathered from whetstones. Often the skins, when

18.text: scraped, have the epidermis left on, which has a natural

19.text: black color, and does not need artificial blackening.
